The '''1974 [[Eliteserien|1. divisjon]]''' was the 30th completed season of Norway's [[Eliteserien|first-tier]] football league and was contested by 12 teams. The season was won by [[Viking FK|Viking]], one point ahead of the newly promoted team [[Molde FK|Molde]]. This was Viking third consecutive league championship, and the fourth total. [[HamKam]], [[Sarpsborg FK|Sarpsborg]] and [[Raufoss IL|Raufoss]] was relegated to the [[1975 2. divisjon]].

==Team changes from 1973==
[[Frigg Oslo FK|Frigg]], [[Lyn Fotball|Lyn]] and [[Fredrikstad FK|Fredrikstad]] was relegated from the [[1973 Norwegian First Division]],<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.rsssf.no/1973/First.html |title=First division 1973 |publisher=RSSSF Norway |access-date=15 March 2013}}</ref> and was replaced by [[Sarpsborg FK|Sarpsborg]] and [[Molde FK|Molde]] who won their [[1973 2. divisjon]] groups, in addition to [[Vålerenga Fotball|Vålerengen]] who won the promotion play-off against [[Bryne FK|Bryne]] and [[FK Mjølner|Mjølner]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.rsssf.no/1973/Second.html |title=Second division 1973 |publisher=RSSSF Norway |access-date=15 March 2013}}</ref>

==Season summary==
Molde, who were playing in the top-flight for the first time since the [[1957–58 Norwegian Main League|1957–58 season]], won their three first matches and were leading the league in 9 of 22 rounds. Molde were in the lead with three matches left to play, despite a 0–2 loss at home against [[Viking FK|Viking]], but when Vålerengen won 4–3 against Molde after a match-winning goal from [[Terje Olsen (footballer born 1950)|Terje Olsen]] in the next match, Viking was the top of the league. Before the last match, Viking was leading one point ahead of Molde, and they won their third consecutive championship after they beat [[Strømsgodset IF|Strømsgodset]] in the last match.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://fotball.rbnett.no/mfk100/article200924.ece |language=no |title=Vi sjokkerte norsk fotball i 1974 |publisher=[[Romsdals Budstikke]] |date=19 May 2011 |access-date=15 March 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120727061059/http://fotball.rbnett.no/mfk100/article200924.ece |archive-date=27 July 2012 }}</ref> Viking had the opportunity to win the [[double (association football)|double]], but lost the [[1974 Norwegian Football Cup]] final 3–1 against [[Skeid Fotball|Skeid]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.skeid.no/nettavisen/2122-bjorge-lillelien-jublet |language=no |title=For 35 år siden... |publisher=Skeid Fotball |date=20 October 2009 |access-date=15 March 2013 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130413233543/http://www.skeid.no/nettavisen/2122-bjorge-lillelien-jublet |archive-date=2013-04-13 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Viking's goalkeeper, [[Erik Johannessen (footballer, born 1952)|Erik Johannessen]] kept a [[clean sheet]] for 672 minutes during the season,<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.vg.no/sport/fotball/norsk/artikkel.php?artid=1235305 |language=no |title=VG vurderer Viking |publisher=Verdens Gang |date=9 April 2001 |access-date=15 March 2012}}</ref> which was a Norwegian record for 32 years until [[Sondre Rossbach]] of [[Odds BK|Odd]] played 730 minutes without conceding a goal in [[2016 Tippeligaen|2016]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.tv2.no/a/8255465/ |language=no |title=Nullen sprakk for Rekord-Rossbach da Friday scoret igjen for LSK |publisher=TV 2 |first=Sturla |last=Johannessen |date=24 April 2016 |access-date=3 June 2018}}</ref> Molde's [[Odd Berg (footballer)|Odd Berg]] became the top goalscorer in the league with 13 goals.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www11.nrk.no/nyheter/distrikt/nrk_trondelag/1.5094796 |language=no |title=Toppscorere |publisher=NRK |first=Tor |last=Berre |date=13 March 2008 |access-date=15 March 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121023080944/http://www.nrk.no/nyheter/distrikt/nrk_trondelag/1.5094796 |archive-date=23 October 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

[[HamKam]], Sarpsborg and [[Raufoss IL|Raufoss]] were relegated at the end of the season.<ref name="rsssf">{{cite web |url=http://www.rsssf.no/1974/First.html |language=no |title=First division 1974 |publisher=RSSSF Norway |access-date=15 March 2012}}</ref> This was HamKam's first relegation from the top league, and the club has later been relegated eight times, which is a Norwegian record.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.nrk.no/nyheter/1.8041146 |language=no |title=HamKam er norgesmestere i nedrykk |publisher=NRK |first=Monica |last=Rikoll |date=19 March 2012 |access-date=15 March 2013}}</ref> Sarpsborg FK had previously been one of the big clubs in Norway, but their spell in the top-flight in 1974 was their last, and for the next 36 years the town of [[Sarpsborg]] did not have a first-tier team until [[Sarpsborg 08 FF|Sarpsborg 08]] played in [[Tippeligaen]] in the [[2011 Norwegian Premier League|2011 season]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://fotball.aftenbladet.no/forstediv/article185062.ece |language=no |title=Sarpsborg rykker opp til eliteserien |publisher=Aftenbladet |agency=Norwegian News Agency |first=Bernhard |last=Veland |date=7 November 2010 |access-date=15 March 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101109121753/http://fotball.aftenbladet.no/forstediv/article185062.ece |archive-date=2010-11-09 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Raufoss, who did not win a match until the 20th round,<ref name="rsssf" /> has not been able to play in the top league again.<ref>{{cite encyclopedia |url=http://snl.no/Raufoss_Idrettslag |language=no |title=Raufoss Idrettslag |encyclopedia=Store norske leksikon |access-date=15 March 2013}}</ref>
